title: Tim Gallaudet Says Guy Who Claims Aliens Built Moon Towers Has Found Atlantis

content:
​A year after UFO disclosure advocate and paranormal enthusiast Tim Gallaudet first claimed that he was on the hunt for Atlantis, the former Naval admiral appeared on Jesse Michels’s American Alchemy podcast, where he alleged that a team that includes a “very wealthy ocean researcher” he won’t name and an ancient astronaut theorist famous for “finding” alien towers on the moon has now found the lost continent:

I'm on an NDA for this. I can't say a whole lot more, but I’m with a team of very esteemed archaeologists and geologists that, uh, we believe we found the region in the Atlantic that fits all the descriptions of Plato’s in Plato’s dialogues where he talks about Atlantis at length. with actual dimensions of the width of the canal and system and other features of it that I won’t go into because I don’t want the location revealed. But we believe we found an area. We have some proprietary bathymetry, and we—it’s very high resolution—and the region that he points to, basically there are a lot of features there that that correspond to exactly how Plato described it.

​Notice that Gallaudet transitioned from finding a place that conforms to “all” of Plato’s description to “a lot” of it. It’s impossible to find a place that will match everything in Plato’s fantasia, and any Atlantis-hunter must by necessity pick and choose what to omit. For instance. Plato describes Atlantis as larger than North Africa (ancient Libya) and Asia Minor combined, something no Atlantis-hunter has ever claimed for a selected site. Similarly, Plato describes it as being outside the Pillars of Hercules (conventionally identified with the Strait of Gibraltar) and sunken beneath an impenetrable layer of mud—another element Atlantis-hunters ignore.

 Gallaudet then explained that the group he joined as an advisor is, essentially, working backward, assuming Plato is literally true and trying to back form a pseudoscientific explanation for the fictitious geology in the story:

I think this whole thing, [the] topic of Atlantis is a lot like UAP, where uh it's just sort of gotten very conflated with all these other theories and whatnot. And I think when you just walk it back to the timeframe he alludes to there, it’s not impossible at all. And then we come up with the geologic theory to explain rapid geological subsidence over a period of just a few years rather than millennia that could cause a whole city to submerge like an island, right? So there’s all the all the physics and all the human history. We’re not talking a million years ago or a billion. We’re talking within the span of human civilization before Egypt.

Gallaudet said that the research is the brainchild of Maaneli (Max) Derakhshani, the physicist who uses AI to “reconstruct” blurry photographs of the moon and then “reveal” supposed “alien” structures in those AI reconstructions. He is now using a similar algorithm to “find” Atlantis. I’m sure this will end well.
